newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks open weaker on last day of account.
newsitem.headline: French stocks open weaker on last day of account.

text.p: French shares started weaker on Monday on the last day of the December account with many investors taking profits.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was down 4.82 points or 0.21 percent at 2,273.71 at 0907 GMT while the CAC-40 futures contract was down at 2,278 from 2,280 on Friday's close.
Rhone-Poulenc's Rorer said it was selling its European vitamin business for $94 million to Hoffmann-La Roche of Switzerland.

Cie de Suez, down 0.19 percent to 212.60, will today receive 5.6 billion francs for the remaining 49 percent in Banque Indosuez from Credit Agricole. The two companies on Saturday announced they were bringing forward the deal which would otherwise have taken place in two steps in 1997 and 2000.
Cie de Suez said it will make a capital gain of 300 million francs on the deal.

Metaleurop falls 7.4 percent to 43.80 francs after announcing a cut in the nominal share value and plans for a 600 million franc capital increase. It also said it returned to profit for the year to September 30.
